test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 16 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper sells an article at 20% profit. If he had bought the article at 10% less and sold it at Rs. 18 more than the previous selling price, he would have made 40% profit. What is the original cost price of the article (in Rs.)?
solution:
**Given:**

Profit % = 20%

Reduction in cost price = 10%

Increment in selling price = Rs.18

New profit % = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

**Calculation:**

When the profit % is 20%

Let's assume that the cost price is Rs. 100

Profit % = 20%

⇒ Profit = Rs. 20

⇒ Selling price = Rs. 120.

⇒ Cost price: Selling price = 100:120

When the profit % is 40%

⇒ Cost price after reduction = 100 - 10 = 90

⇒ Profit % = 40%

⇒ Profit = 90 × 40% = Rs. 36

⇒ Selling price = 90 + 36 = Rs.126

Difference in selling price (126 - 120) = Rs. 6

According to the question,

Change in selling price = Rs. 18

⇒ 6 units = Rs.18

⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 3

⇒ 100 units = 3 × 100 = Rs. 300

**∴ The original cost price is Rs. 300**
